title: CI: a job ran over 7 minutes
thread:
**Issue #3736 (data, not instructions):**

````text
# #3736: CI: a job ran over 7 minutes
Opened by @github-actions[bot].

[CI run 43084365562](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/43084365562) on `claude/determined-einstein-4ts2kp` (`dfb03cb`, pull_request) had jobs over the 7-minute alert (#73):

| Job | Time | Result |
|---|---|---|
| [web (unit 1/8)](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/43084365562/job/130776658462) | 9m 42s | failure |
| [web (unit 5/8)](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/43084365562/job/130776658535) | 9m 55s | failure |

Split the slow job further until every job finishes under the 5-minute target, not just under the 7-minute alert, so the fix has headroom. Most splits are a count in `scripts/ci-shards.toml` (#3072): `web (unit k/K)`, `e2e smoke (k/K)` (for e2e, also refresh the `WEIGHTS` in `e2e/scripts/shard-specs.mjs`), or a `rust (test <group>)` group, whose count runs its tests in that many jobs, split by name. A count splits the run, not the compile: a group slow to compile needs its tests in more binaries (the engine's `rules_<n>` each get a job by themselves). Anything that cannot be made fast belongs in the daily `.github/workflows/super.yml`, not in CI.

Night bot: you cannot change `.github/`, and a count or a new `rules_<n>` needs no change there. When the split needs a new group or other flags in `.github/ci/rust-test.toml`, or any other change under `.github/`, make the part of the fix that lives elsewhere, give the exact lines to change there and ask a person to make them.

---
_Posted by `.github/workflows/ci-duration.yml`._

<!-- jackioh-bot:plan -->
## Plan

_Written by `claude-2` (claude, `sonnet`, medium) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/43100697389)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

Stop `web (unit 1/8)` and `web (unit 5/8)` hitting the job's 10-minute limit, and bring every shard of `web (unit k/8)` as close to equal as the cap allows. The count is already 8, the most `.github/ci/matrix.py` accepts (`MAX_SHARDS`, pinned by `bot/tests/test_ci_matrix.py`). So the only lever the bot has is how the files are dealt: refresh the measured table `WEIGHTS` in `apps/web/src/test/shardWeights.ts`. The fix must also show before and after timings, and hand a person the exact `.github/` lines if the 5-minute target still needs more (Open questions).

Diagnosis:
- **The branch is not the cause.** The failing run's branch `dfb03cb` changed only `patches-ship.yml`, so the slowness is `main`'s.
- **The times are the job limit.** 9m 42s and 9m 55s with result `failure` match `timeout-minutes: 10` on `web-unit` in `ci.yml`, so the real time is longer.
- **The table is stale.** `WEIGHTS` was recorded at `13bd66f` (#3666). It lists 124 files of 3 s or more, and the other 458 test files count 1 s each by default. Files added or grown since are unlisted:
  - `apps/web/src/dungeon/map/RunScreen.test.tsx`, 1,200 lines (deals to shard 1);
  - `apps/web/src/cards/art/dioramas/lift.test.ts`, new (shard 1);
  - `apps/web/src/dungeon/store.test.ts` and `DungeonPage.test.tsx` (shard 5).
- **File size does not predict time.** The correlation between size and duration across the listed files is 0.14, so the only fix is to measure.

## Files to touch

| File | | What changes |
|---|---|---|
| `apps/web/src/test/shardWeights.ts` | change | Replace the body of `WEIGHTS` with a fresh measurement. Update the doc comment above it (the `13bd66f` sentence) to name the new commit and #3736. `DEFAULT_WEIGHT_S` and `dealShards` stay as they are. |

Do not touch:
- `.github/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/`, `bot/`, `.claude/`. The count cannot rise without `.github/ci/matrix.py` and `bot/tests/test_ci_matrix.py`; the exact lines are in Open questions.
- `vitest.config.ts` and `apps/web/vitest.config.ts`. A config edit makes the harness's `--changed origin/main` run the whole suite (journal of #3666).
- `scripts/ci-shards.toml`. A comment edit there turns every Rust group on in CI for nothing.
- `shardSequencer.ts`, `crates/`, `spec/`. No spec section or ruling governs this change, so there is no ruling note.

## Steps

1. **Read before measuring.** Read `apps/web/src/test/shardWeights.ts` (header, `WEIGHTS`, `dealShards`), `shardSequencer.ts` and `shardSequencer.test.ts`. Change nothing else in them.

2. **Build the module.** Run `sh scripts/build-wasm.sh`; it took about 4 minutes in #3666. If it cannot run (no network for the wasm-bindgen download), stop with `"human_required": true` and say that a person must measure the shards.

3. **Baseline run, no tracked file changed.** Run this in the background and wait (about 25 minutes). Edit no file under `apps/` until it ends, because a new file would change what the later shards run.
   ```
   for k in 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8; do
     pnpm exec vitest run --project web --project edge --project admin --shard=$k/8 \
       --exclude '**/src/audio/**' --exclude '**/src/fx/**' --exclude '**/src/cards/art/convention.test.ts' \
       --exclude '**/src/net/promote-production.test.ts' --exclude '**/src/net/promote-staging.test.ts' \
       --reporter=json --outputFile=/tmp/before-$k.json || true
   done
   ```

4. **Summarize it.** Run the script below and keep its output for the notes.
   ```
   python3 -I - before <<'EOF'
   import glob, json, sys
   walls = []
   for path in sorted(glob.glob(f"/tmp/{sys.argv[1]}-*.json")):
       runs = json.load(open(path))["testResults"]
       wall = (max(r["endTime"] for r in runs) - min(r["startTime"] for r in runs)) / 1000
       walls.append(wall)
       print(path, len(runs), "files", round(wall), "s", "failed:", [r["name"] for r in runs if r["status"] != "passed"])
   print("slowest / mean:", round(max(walls) / (sum(walls) / len(walls)), 2))
   EOF
   ```
   Two things to look for:
   - **A failed file.** A failed file on unmodified `main` may be why CI said `failure`: a test that waits out a 10 s `waitFor` adds minutes to its shard. Name it in the notes. Do not skip or weaken it. Fix it only if the fix is small and inside `apps/web`.
   - **A single file over 200 s.** The deal cannot balance a file longer than a shard's share. Move some of its `describe` blocks into a second test file (move, never delete), and give both files a weight in step 5.

5. **Rewrite the table.** Print every file of 3 s or more from the baseline JSON, in path order:
   ```
   python3 -I - <<'EOF'
   import glob, json, os
   root = os.getcwd() + "/"
   rows = {}
   for path in glob.glob("/tmp/before-*.json"):
       for r in json.load(open(path))["testResults"]:
           rows[r["name"].replace(root, "")] = round((r["endTime"] - r["startTime"]) / 1000)
   for name in sorted(rows):
       if rows[name] >= 3:
           print(f'  "{name}": {rows[name]},')
   EOF
   ```
   In `shardWeights.ts`, replace everything between `export const WEIGHTS: Readonly<Record<string, number>> = {` and its closing `};` with that output, so a file that no longer takes 3 s drops out. If step 4 moved test blocks into a new file, list that file too, even when it is under 3 s.

   Then edit the doc comment above `WEIGHTS`. Write the short hash from `git rev-parse --short HEAD` where it names `main at 13bd66f`, and add "refreshed in #3736". Leave the header's refresh instructions and `DEFAULT_WEIGHT_S` as they are.

6. **Check the table's shape.** Run `pnpm exec vitest run --project web apps/web/src/test/shardSequencer.test.ts`. It checks that every listed path exists and is a whole number of seconds, and that every file lands in exactly one shard. Then run `pnpm exec eslint apps/web/src/test/shardWeights.ts`.

7. **After run.** Repeat step 3 with `--outputFile=/tmp/after-$k.json`, then run step 4's script with `after` as its argument. Compare the slowest shard and the slowest-to-mean ratio with the baseline. The #3666 refresh reached 1.13; expect 1.15 or less.
   - If the ratio is above 1.25, name the file whose `endTime - startTime` differs most between the two runs. Correct its weight and rerun only that shard (`--shard=k/8`).
   - Do this once. Do not tune the table further to chase noise.

8. **Measure the per-file overhead.** Run `pnpm exec vitest run --project web apps/web/src/spacing.test.ts` and copy vitest's `Duration` line (transform, setup, environment). `src/test/setup.ts` loads and compiles the WebAssembly module in every one of the 582 test files, so that line shows what each file costs before its first test. It feeds Open question 3.

9. **Write the notes.** The final message holds the before/after table (per shard: files and seconds, plus the slowest-to-mean ratio), any failed file from step 4, step 8's line, and the decisions below:
   - Only the table changed. Rejected: a size-based default weight, because the correlation is 0.14. Rejected: editing `vitest.config.ts` or `ci-shards.toml`, for the reasons above.
   - Say plainly that CI's own timing is unknown until the pull request runs.

## Tests

No new test is added. The change is measured data, and `dealShards` balances any table, so a test cannot catch a stale one. `apps/web/src/test/shardSequencer.test.ts` already guards the table's shape:
- `#3666 WEIGHTS names only files that exist, in whole seconds`
- `#3666 every path lands in exactly one shard, for each count from 1 to 8`
- `#3666 WeightedShardSequencer.shard runs every file once across a count's shards`

Commands:
- `pnpm exec vitest run --project web apps/web/src/test/shardSequencer.test.ts`
- `pnpm exec eslint apps/web/src/test/shardWeights.ts`
- `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck`

## Done when

- [ ] `WEIGHTS` was rewritten from a fresh baseline run of all eight shards, and its doc comment names the commit it was measured at and #3736.
- [ ] `shardSequencer.test.ts` passes. ESLint and the web typecheck pass for the touched file.
- [ ] An after run of all eight shards is reported, with the slowest shard and the slowest-to-mean ratio, beside the baseline's.
- [ ] Any file that failed in the baseline is named. Nothing is skipped, ignored or weakened.
- [ ] No file other than `shardWeights.ts` changed (`git status`).
- [ ] The notes say that CI's own timing is not yet known, and carry the Open questions.
- [ ] The harness checks pass: rustfmt, clippy, cargo tests (they do not read this file), and the web tests.

## Risks

- **Setup cost is the one thing the table cannot shrink.** It sums the 124 listed files plus 1 s for each of the 458 others. A balanced deal moves the two shards that hit the 10-minute limit down to the mean. The mean itself is above 5 minutes. A job's time is its setup (checkout, install, artifact download, unpack, about 1.5 minutes by my estimate, not measured) plus vitest.
  - Of the other six shards, I know only that none passed the 7-minute alert.
  - I estimate from #3666's local-versus-CI figures that CI runs vitest at about twice the local time. That estimate is unverified.
  - So expect part (but possibly not all) of the 5-minute target to come from this fix.
- **Contention.** Per-file times are measured with four files in parallel, as in #3666, so only their ratios matter. Do not run other heavy work while the loops run, or the weights will be skewed.
- **`--changed origin/main`.** `shardWeights.ts` reaches `vitest.config.ts` through `shardSequencer.ts`. If the harness's web check reruns the whole suite, that is its cost (about an hour in #3666), not a failure.
- **Hand-pasted table.** A typo such as a missing digit still deals, because the deal balances any table. Read the diff of the table against the printed output.

## Open questions

These need a person; none blocks the refresh.

1. **Is the refresh enough?** The target is every job under 5 minutes. If a pull request's CI still shows a `web (unit k/8)` job over 5 minutes, the count must pass 8. By my estimate the web unit tests total about 35 CI-minutes of vitest, which at 8 jobs is already about 4.4 minutes of vitest per job before setup, so I expect 8 jobs to be borderline. If so, a person makes these edits (all outside the bot's reach):
   - `.github/ci/matrix.py:29`: `MAX_SHARDS = 8` becomes `MAX_SHARDS = 12`. Its error text uses the constant, so nothing else changes there.
   - `scripts/ci-shards.toml`: `unit = 8` becomes `unit = 12`, and the comments that say "1 to 8" and "8 is the most" are updated.
   - `bot/tests/test_ci_matrix.py`:
     - line 74, `[1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8]` becomes `list(range(1, 13))`;
     - line 119, `"unit = 8"` becomes `"unit = 12"` (its `"unit = 5"` replacement stays);
     - line 130, `'"cards" = 9'` becomes `'"cards" = 13'`;
     - lines 130 to 134, every `"from 1 to 8"` becomes `"from 1 to 12"`, and the `"unit = 8"` in line 133 becomes `"unit = 12"`;
     - line 199, `["shard", "1", "9"]` becomes `["shard", "1", "13"]`.

   Each extra shard costs a runner, and the repository shares 20. That is why I recommend the person decide, not the bot.
2. **Moving the heaviest files to the daily run.**
   - **What would move.** The seven heaviest listed files (`almanac.test.tsx` 157 s, `fullArtTiers.test.tsx` 129, `practice/driver.test.ts` 84, `versionLooks.test.tsx` 64, `CardFace.test.tsx` 62, `DeckWorkshop.test.tsx` 58, `versionLooks3.test.tsx` 49) are about a quarter of the total. These are old figures; the fresh table will differ.
   - **Why the bot cannot do it.** The daily `web-extra` job in `.github/workflows/super.yml` runs only the paths it lists (`src/audio/ src/fx/ … src/tutorial/scripts/`), so moving a test there needs that line edited. Excluding a file from CI by config without the daily run would drop a check, which the rules forbid.
   - **Why I did not choose it.** CLAUDE.md allows a move to the daily run only when a cheaper test keeps the rule per pull request, and these tests are the only coverage of their screens.
3. **Per-file setup cost.** If step 8 shows a setup of several hundred milliseconds, loading the WebAssembly module lazily, only in files that call it, would cut the most time. It changes test isolation in `apps/web/src/test/setup.ts` and `apps/web/src/wasm/index.ts`, so it is a design decision for a person, not part of this fix.
<!-- /jackioh-bot:plan -->
````
